short: A massive, decisive Yorkist victory that secured the throne for Edward IV during the Wars of the Roses.
full:
Fought on Palm Sunday in a blinding snowstorm on 29 March 1461, the Battle of Towton is widely considered the largest and bloodiest battle ever fought on English soil. The Yorkist army, led by the newly proclaimed Edward IV, met a massive Lancastrian force in Yorkshire.

After hours of brutal hand-to-hand combat, the Lancastrian line broke. Thousands were killed in the ensuing rout, effectively destroying the Lancastrian field army. The catastrophic defeat secured Edward's grip on the throne and forced Henry VI, Margaret of Anjou, and their remaining supporters to flee into exile in Scotland.
